_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. These are spec-shape-triggered PSA gotchas; the next PSA reprint (connectwise-manage, halopsa) will hit several again.

handfixes.summary: The Autotask entity 'Resources' syncs and stores its rows: 4.34.2 renders no typed `resources` table, so the collision with the framework's generic `resources` store table (and its FTS trigger crash) cannot occur; the e2e test syncs `resources` through the real CLI and reads the stored rows back
handfixes.why: Autotask has an entity literally named 'Resources'. The generator emits a typed table `resources` that collides with the framework's generic `resources` store table; 4.22's typed-FTS triggers then crash EVERY sync insert (`resources_fts has no column named name`). The generator shadow-renames colliding Cobra commands but NOT store tables, so the typed Resources table was hand-renamed to `psa_resources` (with its FTS index, triggers, backfill, typed upsert, SearchX, and upgrade test). Restated on the 4.34.2 reprint: the generator no longer emits a typed Resources table (no `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS resources (` beside the generic store), so the psa_resources rename has nothing to rename. The assert is now the behaviour (rows synced and stored) and the absence of the colliding table.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should shadow-rename a typed store table that collides with a reserved/generic framework table (filed via printing-press-retro).

handfixes.summary: The composed-apiKey header-blanking bug must stay fixed: client must NOT re-Set UserName/Secret to empty after setting them
handfixes.why: The 4.22 generated client.go emitted unconditional `req.Header.Set("UserName", ""); req.Header.Set("Secret", "")` resets right after setting the sibling apiKey credentials, blanking them -> all live calls 401. The hand-fix removes the reset lines (the buggy pattern now survives only as an explanatory NOTE comment, pinned by autotask_headers_test.go) and sets the real values. NOTE: the literal blanked-Set string intentionally remains inside the explanatory comment, so this entry asserts the FIX (the documenting comment + the real value-Sets) rather than banning a substring that legitimately appears in the comment.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press must stop emitting empty-string header resets for composed-apiKey schemes (filed via printing-press-retro).

handfixes.summary: CheckRedirect deletes ALL custom auth headers (ApiIntegrationCode + sibling UserName/Secret) before a cross-host redirect, not just the primary
handfixes.why: Go's default cross-host redirect handling strips only standard auth; the generated CheckRedirect deleted only the PRIMARY custom header, so sibling apiKey headers (UserName/Secret) forwarded verbatim to cross-host redirect targets -> credential leak. The hand-fix adds the extra Header.Del calls for the sibling credentials.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press CheckRedirect should delete every custom auth header for composed-apiKey schemes on cross-host hops.

handfixes.summary: Novel commands renamed/registered to avoid framework-name collisions: generic newStaleCmd (pm_stale.go) dropped, novel `data-gaps` keeps a unique name
handfixes.why: The 4.22 novel-stub emitter re-emits framework-named commands alongside same-name novels (dup-cobra, first-added wins). pm_stale.go (generic data-layer `stale`) collided with the hand-built novel `stale`; pm_stale.go was deleted and its registration dropped (the transcendence spec keeps the novel impl). The novel aggregation was named `data-gaps` (not a framework name like pm_orphans' `orphans`). A reprint must not re-register the generic newStaleCmd (the root.go comment documents the dropped registration) and must keep the unique `data-gaps` name. (The gate cannot assert pm_stale.go's absence directly - it asserts the documenting comment + the data-gaps name/registration instead.)
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press novel-stub emitter must not emit a stub whose name collides with a declared novel/framework command.

handfixes.summary: Hand-written novel aggregations pass math.MaxInt32 to store.List so they are not silently capped at 200 rows
handfixes.why: store.List(rt, 0) silently means LIMIT 200, not unlimited (same unabsorbed press gap as sherweb/pax8). Every hand-written novel that aggregates across the fleet must pass math.MaxInt32 or it truncates at 200 rows and reports wrong PSA rollups.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Fix store.List limit<=0 semantics in the press (no cap means no cap).

handfixes.summary: POST-query sync seeds the id-walk filter on the FIRST page (`id gte 0`) and coerces array/CSV body params, so page 1 is never sent filterless
handfixes.why: Autotask's query endpoints require a filter: a filterless body answers HTTP 500 "Value cannot be null. Parameter name: filters", so every POST sync resource failed on its first page and synced nothing (issue #257). The press emits syncResourceStaticBody entries only for body fields carrying an OpenAPI `default`, and Autotask's `filter` declares none, so the generated static body is empty and appendIDWalkFilter ran only once a cursor already existed. The seed is the walk's own `id gte 0` condition, NOT an empty array: Autotask matches records against the filter conditions, so `filter: []` returns HTTP 200 with zero rows and turns a loud failure into a silent empty sync. coerceSyncBodyParam also gained the array/string_csv_array cases the generated query commands already had, so a --param override reaches the wire as JSON instead of the literal string "[...]".
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press should seed the id-walk filter param on the first page of any POST-query sync whose body declares a required filter array (or emit a static body for required array params with no default), and coerceSyncBodyParam should decode array/string_csv_array the way the generated query commands do (filed via printing-press-retro).

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For autotask the manifest gained: AUTOTASK_BASE_URL. server.json gained: AUTOTASK_API_INTEGRATION_CODE, AUTOTASK_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: AUTOTASK_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name; applied by tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py. The <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed; teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. A write that repeats a held credential (the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl, profiles.json and the learn tables) is the shared credential kit's: its file sinks and SQL driver withhold it. journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 and 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) return the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included, and record every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query; and a credential given as a profile name or description, a recall or teach query or operand, or feedback is stored as typed. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment; operator-named text that repeats no credential the process holds is a name and is kept. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; re-run tools/maintainer/apply_journal_hardening.py --slug <slug>.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

Cmd:           journalVerbChain(rootCmd, executed),
		ArgvShape:     learn.JournalArgvShape(os.Args[1:], isBoolFlag, isDeclaredFlag),
writeTeachErrLog(fmt.Sprintf("teach: missing --query (%d args, %d resources)", len(args), len(resources)))

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. Ported to autotask from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Installed on every CLI, novel and MCP client by registerClientHook (internal/cli/autotask_guard.go), with the response cache off and --dry-run clients refusing every send
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: the generated client sends the ApiIntegrationCode header to whatever URL it is handed and its CheckRedirect strips only the named auth headers, so a Location to another host or an absolute path from an MCP argument would carry the key off the vendor API. One origin, taken from the configured base URL; an operator who sets AUTOTASK_BASE_URL moves the pin with it. Ported to autotask from the atera 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: doctorShippedBaseURL is empty: the shipped default (https://webservices5.autotask.net/atservicesrest/V1.0) is a real Autotask zone host, so doctor probes it instead of reporting a zone-5 tenant's correct install as an unconfigured placeholder
handfixes.why: press-traps s5: the fleet doctor replay restored doctor_verdict.go with doctorShippedBaseURL naming webservices5, so doctor printed "not configured (base_url is a placeholder)" and skipped the credential probe for every tenant in zone 5. Every webservicesN.autotask.net host is a real zone. The template / YOUR_ / reserved-domain rules still apply. TestDoctorProbesTheRealAutotaskZoneHosts was seen failing on the replayed file (seen/doctor-real-host-seen-failing.log). tools/apply_edits.py re-applies it; a fleet re-mint of the doctor template would restore the placeholder value: keep this entry.

handfixes.summary: zone asks only the fixed bootstrap origin (https://webservices.autotask.net) with the origin pin installed, saves a discovered URL only when it is https://webservicesN.autotask.net[:443]/atservicesrest[/v1.0] (config.ValidateZoneURL: no userinfo, query or fragment), sends the UserName (from --user, AUTOTASK_USERNAME or AUTOTASK_PSA_USER_NAME; the API user's login name, an Identifier in the credwire Declarations, not held) nowhere else, and over MCP previews (--no-save) until confirm
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: zone sends the API user's name to the bootstrap host and saves the URL it answers with as the base URL every later call sends the integration code and the Secret to. Unpinned, a redirect or a zoneInformation answer naming another host would move every credential there on the next call. Seen failing: seen/zone-hardening-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: spec.json lists the three auth headers (ApiIntegrationCode, UserName, Secret) only as securityDefinitions, never as per-operation parameters, so 4.34.2 renders no required --api-integration-code/--user-name/--secret flags, keeps every command's Example, and emits no unconditional UserName/Secret resets
handfixes.why: The vendor spec repeats the three auth headers as required header parameters on every operation (2925 of them). 4.24 ignored them; 4.34.2 renders each as a required credential FLAG (a credential on the command line), drops the Cobra Example of every command whose required inputs it cannot derive (1069 commands, dogfood examples 1/10), and emits `req.Header.Set("UserName", "")` / `req.Header.Set("Secret", "")` after the sibling credentials are set, so every call would 401. tools/spec_fix.py (run dir) drops header params named by a header securityDefinition before the render; spec-encoded, so a reprint keeps it as long as the spec repair runs.

handfixes.summary: Every novel reads the store through listEntity, which refuses a resource whose rows are not backed by a finished sync (a sync that stopped part way, a filtered walk, or rows a live read wrote through with no sync) and a resource never synced in a store where others were, and names the sync to run
handfixes.why: Class incomplete-snapshot-read-as-complete (Codex r1 P1 on the shared layer's atera and liongard prints, pre-closed here): every live read writes through to the store, a sync that stops part way leaves last_attempt_complete = 0, and `sync --resources tickets --param filter=[...status eq 5]` finishes as a complete walk, so triage / ticket-aging / company-360 / account-brief answered from a partial store and read missing records as absent. handfixes.why: Codex r1 P1: account-brief read an opportunity's lastActivityDate/lastActivityDateTime, which OpportunityModel does not carry (its field is lastActivity), so every opportunity moved in the window was left out. The class test also removed the other undocumented reads (ticket createdDate/lastActivityDateTime/dueDate, project endDate/title, task dueDate/percentComplete, contract-block hoursLeft/hoursRemaining/hoursUsed, time-entry invoiceID/hours). Seen failing: seen/r1-wrong-field-read-from-a-documented-response-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: the first unfiltered walk after any recorded filtered walk starts from no cursor and only then marks its own cursor resumable (autotask_sync_unfiltered_resume), so a store filled by a build without the mark restarts too
handfixes.why: Codex r2 P1 (class incomplete-snapshot-read-as-complete, repeat; fixed after the stop rule, not re-reviewed): the r1 mark was written by the filtered walk, so a store from the r1 build had no mark, the unfiltered walk resumed after cursor 101 and triage omitted ticket 1. Seen failing: seen/r2-recorded-filtered-cursor-resumed-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: tail's later polls ask for higher ids plus the records modified since the newest modification time seen (tailChangeField, checked against spec.json), walk every page for a resource with none, and emit only new or changed records
handfixes.why: Codex r2 P1 (class documented-updates-omitted; fixed after the stop rule, not re-reviewed): later polls asked only for id > the highest emitted, so a ticket completed after the first poll was never emitted. Seen failing: seen/r2-tail-updates-omitted-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: a checkpoint written without the filtered-walk record (an older build, or workflow archive) counts as a possibly filtered walk: the novels refuse it and the next unfiltered sync starts that resource over
handfixes.why: Codex r2 class incomplete-snapshot-read-as-complete, older store (found while fixing the r2 input; fixed after the stop rule, not re-reviewed): the published 4.24 build kept no filtered-walk record, so its filtered sync left a complete checkpoint and this build's triage trusted it, omitting every unmatched ticket. Seen failing: seen/r2-store-without-filter-record-trusted-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own holder, output chokepoint, funnel and withholding SQL driver. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal (the integration code and Secret headers, the config and store fields, --stdin, the response credential members, the MCP arguments, every source of the API user name as an Identifier, and where each credential may go: the base URL, the MCP HTTP token nowhere); each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; the API, zone, feedback, deliver and probe clients go through credkit.Transport (client.OutboundGuard, under the api-origin-pinned origin pin); every file write outside the 0600 credential store and the config goes through the kit; the MCP stdio server passes credkit.MCPIn, MCPOut and MCPTools; MCP children run through credkit.RunCommand.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. Replaced by the kit and removed from this ledger (each replaced by the shared credential kit): secret-echo-decoded-funnel, output-chokepoint, file-sinks-withheld, store-never-keeps-secrets, mcp-protocol-messages-withheld, network-sinks-withheld, startup-output-held-first, mcp-held-arguments-refused, undecoded-encodings-every-alignment, held-forms-in-every-encoding, response-credentials-held, every-text-encoding-withheld, outbound-split-parts-refused, auth-carrier-names-and-shapes-held, secure-container-is-credential, r1-holder-reads-every-part, r1-mixed-byte-escapes-decoded, r1-split-across-deliveries-withheld, held-value-case-folded, output-units-reassembled, preclose-holder-numbers-and-cookies, preclose-escape-fixpoint, preclose-split-across-processes-and-protocol, refuse-held-uses-connector-chokepoint, output-derived-and-scheme-forms-matched-whole, g304-paths-cleaned-not-annotated, r1-short-value-encodings-withheld, r1-file-history-is-the-whole-file, r2-short-value-nested-encodings, r1-credential-split-across-deliveries, r1-decoder-bound-read-as-no-echo, r1-persistence-gate-narrower-than-chokepoint, startup-error-lost, spec-names-pinned, own-metadata-not-held, r1-raw-deflate-inflated, r1-file-store-keys-held, r1-holder-reads-named-config, r1-agentcookie-config-holds-no-credential, r2-raw-deflate-trailing-bytes, r2-holder-parses-the-command-flags, r2-broken-toml-values-held. Retired, not replaced (the API user name is a declared identifier: the Autotask UserName is the API user's login name, an email address in the tenant's own domain that Autotask answers repeat, so it is exempt with a reason under contract section 1, and the integration code and Secret stay the credentials): user-name-held-by-value. Tests: internal/credwire/leak_test.go and internal/autotaskblackbox/kit_classes_test.go and user_name_identifier_test.go on the built binaries, each seen failing with the wiring disabled.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring and the Declarations literal.

handfixes.summary: Every SQLite handle goes through credkit.SQLDriver: internal/credsql registers the one driver and every sql.Open in store.go and platform/migration.go names it, the read-only opener included. The MCP sql value cap is a DSN parameter credsql applies as each connection opens (OpenReadOnlyValueCapped), not sqlite.Limit on a held connection. The read-only opener runs select 1 because the kit's connection does not forward Ping. It replaces the connector's own withholding driver.
handfixes.why: A statement's text and bound values are a sink of their own, reads included.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate store, migration and MCP sql opens against one kit-wrapped driver name, and express the MCP sql value cap as a connection-open setting.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing, then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the inner, kit-wrapped handler and only a write-free preflight runs before credkit.MCPHTTP.

handfixes.summary: credentialFiles returns the config the program really uses first, because the kit takes the base URL and every allowed origin from the first file naming one: an explicit --config or AUTOTASK_CONFIG wins, the last --home decides the default paths, and every other file any flag could mean is only held. The credential stores and run profile stores are only held: config.Load takes no base URL from a store. Startup reads --config and --home by their last occurrence (credkit.FlagValues); the root pre-run refuses a run whose parsed values differ (another flag swallowed one). autotask-mcp, which has no such flags, refuses to start when startup read one.
handfixes.why: A discovered default's base_url must not become an allowed origin for a credential from another file.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the file discovery in the wiring file.

handfixes.summary: --stdin is a declared StdinFlag, so the kit holds a body whole and line by line before anything prints. cliutil.CompactStdinBody puts a JSON body on one line first, because a line of { alone collides with public text and refuses the start. feedback --stdin refuses instead of reporting a record the kit would withhold.
handfixes.why: A hand-written body parser was a second reader of what the kit already holds. The cost is recorded in the docs: a preview of a --stdin body, and an answer repeating part of it, are withheld, and the write still happens.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate StdinFlags and the compaction with the kit wiring.

handfixes.summary: The spec's credential members (a webhook's secretKey, a client-portal user's password, an integration vendor insight's or widget's secret) are replaced by name with [withheld] in every response and dry-run body (client.maskCredentialFields), so a listing that carries one stays usable; the kit holds the same names as ResponseFields and CredentialFields.
handfixes.why: The kit withholds a whole unit that carries a held value; replacing the member by name first keeps the rest of the record readable.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the response credential members from the spec's secret-shaped properties.

handfixes.summary: The run profile store (profiles.json) is a credential source: credwire.credentialFiles holds it at startup and the profile loader holds it again before parsing, both with credkit.HoldBody, so a value under a declared credential name (secret, ApiIntegrationCode, a config field) or base-url is held, every duplicate included.
handfixes.why: A decoder keeps the last of a duplicate key; the kit's body reader holds every occurrence before any command reads the store.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the profile store hold in the wiring file and the profile loader.

handfixes.summary: tail's id and modification-time cursors move only when a poll reads every page of every pass (the id cursor only on the walk by id); a record is marked emitted only after emit returns, so a poll that stops part-way reads the same window again
handfixes.why: Codex r1 (4.34.2 kit review) P1: the cursors moved page by page, so a poll cut off by a 401 on its second page kept the newest modification time of the page it read and every later poll skipped an update with an earlier time on the page it never read. Seen failing: .review/seen/fix2-tail-watermark-seen-failing.txt.

handfixes.summary: migrate runs only the CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS statements whose object (same sqlite_master type and name) is missing (pendingMigrations); a statement it cannot name runs as before; what is left runs as one multi-statement Exec (execMigrations), so the kit checks one unit
handfixes.why: Every store open ran about 480 no-op CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS statements, and the credential kit's SQL driver checks each statement's text, so with a credential held one open cost about 5 s of CPU (0.7 s after the fix) and the black-box suite passed go test's 10 minute limit on the 4-vCPU CI runners (PR #565). Seen: .review/seen/store-open-cpu-before-after.txt.
